mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in federal funds rates over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -0.5% AND HOUST falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both GDPC1 YoY < -0.5% and HOUST declines for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5% for two consecutive months signals labor market softening, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE exceeds 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.8% for three consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when INDPRO declines by more than 0.8% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth above 0.5% month-over-month, combined with a stable unemployment rate, signals robust labor market expansion that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when PAYEMS grows > 0.5% MoM and UNRATE is stable.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 0.6% for four consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when RSAFS rises by more than 0.6% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in CPIAUCSL below 2% for three consecutive months, combined with stable or declining FEDFUNDS, signals a loosening monetary environment with low inflation risk, which supports equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% for 3 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS not rising
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when CPIAUCSL < 2% for three months and FEDFUNDS is stable or declining.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,200,000 units for four consecutive months signals a housing market downturn that reduces construction-related economic activity and drags on equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when HOUST remains below 1,200,000 for four consecutive months.
